title: 'The G Engines Are Coming' article arrives on Cook's desk

tellings.quote: there was an article that showed up on my desk. I mean, people would send stuff to us at Jane's.
there's a really interesting article from 1956 called the G engines are coming or something like that.
tellings.difference: Leaves out Cook and credits Gladish, Deser and Arnowitt instead of Trimble.
tellings.link_reason: The same 1956 'The G Engines Are Coming' article as the story where it reaches Cook at Jane's.

plain: The story is about an old magazine article called "The G Engines Are Coming," which by its title promised engines that could master gravity. A journalist named Nick Cook, who worked at Jane's Defence Weekly, a British military trade publication, says the article simply "showed up on my desk," because people often sent material to Jane's. For Cook it was a sign that serious people in the aircraft industry once openly worked on antigravity, and he ties it to a man named George S. Trimble. Michels brings up the same article in a later episode, dating it to 1956 and calling it "really interesting." He leaves Cook out and instead links it to people named Michael Gladish, Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt. Cook tells it as something he handled himself, while Michels tells it as something he has read about. If the article meant what its title says, it would show antigravity research was being discussed in the open in the 1950s before it went quiet.
